summary: Reports that the Lincoln Laboratory 360/67 passed testing of its network software, including the NCP, ICP, Telnet as user and server, login, CMS access, and operator communication. Everything behaved according to specs. It updates RFC 193 and was replaced by RFC 214.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 198 reports a test of Lincoln Laboratory's 360/67 network software. The systems behaved according to their specifications, including under moderate to heavy load.

subtitle: A short report says Lincoln Laboratory's 360/67 network software passed its checks.

tldr.problem: Network participants needed to know whether Lincoln Laboratory's host software behaved according to current specifications.
tldr.mechanism: The report says engineers exercised NCP, ICP, ASCII Telnet in user and server roles, login, CMS access, and operator and console communication.
tldr.outcome: The report says the software behaved according to specifications and multiple message responses remained smooth under moderate to heavy load. RFC 198 was later obsoleted by RFC 214.

today: RFC 198 was obsoleted by RFC 214 and updates RFC 193. It records a short test report for the Lincoln Laboratory 360/67.

sections.title: Testing the Lincoln Laboratory Host
sections.content: RFC 198 reports that Lincoln Laboratory's network software was exercised. The report names the host as the Lincoln Labs 360/67 and states that its tested components behaved according to current specifications.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a short report on tests of the 360/67's network software. The report says the tested components worked as specified.

sections.title: What the Test Covered
sections.content: The test covered NCP, ICP, ASCII Telnet as both a user and a server, the login procedure, access to CMS, and operator and console communication. The report also says that multiple message responses, such as listing users, were smooth under moderate to heavy load.
sections.plainLanguage: The test included network control, connection setup, Telnet, login, CMS access, and operator communication. It also checked multiple responses while the machine was busy.

sections.title: Reported Result
sections.content: The author states that the exercised software behaved according to the current specifications and that multiple message responses were smooth under moderate to heavy load. RFC 198 updates RFC 193 and was later obsoleted by RFC 214, according to the unit metadata.
sections.plainLanguage: The report records successful behavior for the tested software. It updates RFC 193 and was later replaced by RFC 214.
